title: Sweep atomicwrite users that tmp+rename linkable .evolve/ state files without resolving the worktree symlink (cycle-999 sever class)
evidence: Follow-up of statejson-latent-unresolved-writers how_to_apply step (3). Cycle 1690 delivered steps (1) and (2): statemap.ResolveWriteTarget is exported, core.SealCycle locks the resolved <canonical>.lock, and failurelog's atomicWriteJSON seam renames onto the resolved target.

Step (3) was deferred in scout prose only (triage-decision.json deferred: []), and a PASS landing consumes the whole lane item through ship/postship.go committedInboxIDs. This record carries step (3) forward so it does not vanish with the parent (cycle-1690 audit M1).

Cycle-1690 Discovery Scan: other atomicwrite callers write .evolve/ state-adjacent files. Any of them reached with a worktree-linked path would replace the link with a regular file, the cycle-999 sever.
how_to_apply: (1) Enumerate every atomicwrite caller whose target can be a worktree-linked .evolve/ file (state.json and its siblings the worktree provisioner symlinks). (2) For each one, route the write through statemap.ResolveWriteTarget, or add an opt-in resolve-symlinks mode to atomicwrite and use it at those sites. (3) Pin each migrated writer with a symlink regression test that mirrors statemap_integrity_test.go.
acceptance: A written inventory lists every atomicwrite caller in go/ whose target path can be a worktree-linked .evolve/ state file, and marks each one migrated or not-linkable with a reason.

Every caller marked linkable writes through the resolved target (statemap.ResolveWriteTarget or an atomicwrite resolve mode): after the write the symlink is still a symlink and the canonical file holds the new bytes.
Each migrated writer has a regression test that fails on the pre-fix code, covering an absolute link, a relative link and a dangling link.
